verdict.rationale: The API docs say you can try the API in the browser playground and use Console workspaces to separate environments, so a test workspace can be kept apart from production. That separation is thinly documented, and there is no dedicated sandbox or test mode with isolated mock data. The sandboxed code-execution container isolates code execution, not a test environment, so it is not credited. Missing for 10: a dedicated sandbox or test mode with isolated non-production data, in-depth docs on workspace-based environment isolation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Use workspaces in the Console to separate environments and control spend by use case.
In the Console, you can use playground (platform.claude.com/playground) to try out the API in the browser and then generate API keys on the API keys page
